title: CP-SAT chromatic / fanout structural filter on N1 candidates
hypothesis: K4 is a k-alphabet per-position substitution; candidate plaintexts with fanout>k are impossible
best_partial: min fanout 7; 0 candidates admissible at k<=4
insights: Fanout lower-bound distribution over 5220 N1 candidates: {7: 5, 8: 134, 9: 619, 10: 1254, 11: 1415, 12: 1034, 13: 506, 14: 184, 15: 53, 16: 12, 17: 2, 18: 1, 22: 1}. Minimum fanout = 7 (=> EVERY candidate needs >= 7 alphabets for a per-position cipher to K4).
Admissible at k<=4: 0; k<=5: 0; k<=6: 0 (out of 5220).
Exact CP-SAT chromatic number on the 30 lowest-fanout candidates: {7: 3, 8: 27}.

STRUCTURAL RULING: a K=4 per-position substitution requires a plaintext where every letter maps to <=4 distinct K4 letters. The minimum any N1 candidate achieves is 7. Real English (K1 plaintext) fanout vs a random target is 14. => the true K4 plaintext (if K<=4) is FAR more repetition-constrained than any natural-English N1 candidate -- strong evidence that either the prior misses the real plaintext OR K4 is NOT a low-k per-position cipher.
next_steps: the fanout result is a HARD constraint on the true plaintext: search/generate ONLY plaintexts with per-letter fanout<=4 against K4 (a strong new N1 filter); feed those to exp 054
if no plausible English has fanout<=4, that argues K4's masking is NOT per-position substitution -- revisit transposition-composite families
